sentences.text: Not every tow is behind the tug.
On the Intracoastal you’ll mostly see barges pushed ahead, or lashed alongside.
When a pushing vessel and the vessel she pushes are rigidly connected as a composite unit, they count as one power-driven vessel, and show ordinary Rule twenty-three lights.
From ahead, a vessel pushing ahead or towing alongside shows two masthead lights in a vertical line, and sidelights.
From astern is where the two rule books split.
Under the International rules, she shows a sternlight.
Under the Inland rules, she shows two yellow towing lights in a vertical line instead.
So picture yourself overtaking something big and slow on the Intracoastal at night, and all you see is two yellow lights, one above the other.
A towboat pushing ahead or towing alongside, under Inland rules.
And one more Inland detail: on the Western Rivers and certain other waters, a vessel pushing ahead or towing alongside shows sidelights and the two towing lights, with no masthead lights at all.
